s1.syndrome_frame: asymptomatic cardiac abnormality with systolic murmur and abnormal ECG findings in a young pregnant woman
salient_findings: systolic murmur in the left upper parasternal region
complete right bundle-branch block with fragmented QRS on ECG
dilated right atrium and right ventricle with large defect on echocardiography
key_facts: 29-year-old primigravida woman
no history of dyspnea, chest pain, palpitation, or lower limb swelling
vital parameters within normal limits
systolic murmur in the left upper parasternal region
normal sinus rhythm with heart rate of 70 beats/min on ECG
complete right bundle-branch block with normal PR interval on ECG
fragmented QRS with a notch on the R wave in inferior leads on ECG
no significant ST-T segment changes on ECG
dilated right atrium and right ventricle on transthoracic echocardiography
large 21-mm defect with left-to-right shunt on transthoracic echocardiography
normal cardiac output on right-sided heart catheterization
step-up in oxygenation from superior vena cava to right atrium
pulmonary vascular resistance: 1.8 Wood units

raw.rationale: The presence of a systolic murmur, dilated right atrium and right ventricle, and a large 21-mm defect with left-to-right shunt on transthoracic echocardiography, along with a step-up in oxygenation from the superior vena cava to the right atrium, are all consistent with a ventricular septal defect.

rejected.why: While the ECG shows a complete right bundle-branch block, this is not the primary diagnosis that explains the key facts, including the systolic murmur and the large defect with left-to-right shunt.

rejected.label: right bundle branch block
rejected.why: Similar to complete right bundle branch block, this is a finding on the ECG but does not explain the structural heart defect indicated by the echocardiography and catheterization findings.

rejected.label: mitral regurgitation
rejected.why: There is no mention of mitral valve issues or regurgitation in the provided key facts or diagnostic findings.

rejected.label: hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The findings do not indicate hypertrophy of the heart muscle, and the primary issue appears to be a structural defect rather than muscle thickening or hypertrophy.
